output.summary: The problem is that high-consumption AMI register reads are rejected during billing import, causing disputed bills. This was established by evidence showing most disputed estimated bills have AMI reads rejected for high consumption (E-11), dispute volume rose from ~610 to ~1,260 tickets (E-04), and disputed bills have more actual than estimated reads (E-02), indicating the root cause is not missing reads. The released capability flags high-consumption AMI reads in the billing system for review (DA-BILL). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the Define gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring threshold optimization as VOB-U-U3, allowing release with known limitation. Known limitations are that the optimal high-consumption threshold remains undefined (VOB-U-U3 open) and adjustments to billing import rules or monitoring are deferred outside this release.
